resources.title: Counting, permutations, and combinations (Unit 8)
resources.why_recommended: Complete, exercise-backed unit that builds counting intuition from the fundamental counting principle through permutations and combinations, with practice problems ideal for GATE prep.

resources.title: Probability and Statistics (NPTEL) - Combinatorics & Counting lectures
resources.why_recommended: Rigorous Indian-curriculum treatment of counting and classical probability from IIT Kharagpur, well aligned with the GATE syllabus and exam style.

topics.topic_name: Probability Axioms, Sample Space & Events (incl. mutually exclusive / independent events)

resources.title: RES.6-012 Introduction to Probability - Unit 1: Probability Models and Axioms
resources.why_recommended: The gold-standard rigorous introduction: sample space, axioms of probability, and events taught precisely by Tsitsiklis, with videos, notes, and problem sets.

resources.title: Probability and Statistics (NPTEL) - Sample space, events and axioms
resources.why_recommended: GATE-aligned NPTEL lecture series that develops probability axioms, mutually exclusive and independent events in the style expected on the exam.

resources.title: Statistics 110: Probability - Lectures 1-3 (Probability, Sets, Independence)
resources.why_recommended: Blitzstein's legendary Stat 110 opens with sample space, axioms, and independence, giving deep conceptual intuition alongside rigor.

resources.title: Conditional Probability, Clearly Explained!!!
resources.why_recommended: StatQuest's crystal-clear visual explanation of conditional probability, ideal first exposure before tackling GATE-level problems.

resources.title: Statistics 110: Probability - Conditional Probability & Independence lectures
resources.why_recommended: Blitzstein's treatment of conditioning (the 'soul of statistics'), the multiplication rule, and independence with memorable examples.

resources.title: RES.6-012 Introduction to Probability - Conditioning and Independence
resources.why_recommended: Rigorous MIT coverage of conditional probability, the total probability theorem, and independence with worked problem sets.

resources.title: Bayes' Theorem, Clearly Explained!!!!
resources.why_recommended: StatQuest breaks Bayes' theorem into intuitive pieces, making posterior updating easy to grasp before GATE numericals.

resources.title: Bayes theorem, the geometry of changing beliefs
resources.why_recommended: 3Blue1Brown's geometric intuition for Bayes' theorem builds deep understanding of why the formula works, complementing StatQuest.

resources.title: The quick proof of Bayes' theorem
resources.why_recommended: A short, clean derivation of Bayes' theorem that cements the algebra behind the intuition.

resources.title: RES.6-012 Introduction to Probability - Discrete Random Variables & Multiple RVs
resources.why_recommended: Definitive coverage of random variables, joint PMFs/PDFs, and marginalization, with clear notation and problem sets matching GATE depth.

resources.title: Statistics 110: Probability - Joint, Conditional, and Marginal Distributions
resources.why_recommended: Blitzstein's lectures on joint distributions and random variables give the intuition and worked examples GATE aspirants need.

topics.topic_name: Descriptive Statistics (mean, median, mode, standard deviation, variance)

resources.title: Estimating the Mean, Variance, and Standard Deviation, Clearly Explained!!!
resources.why_recommended: StatQuest clarifies the difference between population and sample estimates of mean, variance, and standard deviation, a common GATE stumbling block.

resources.title: Summarizing quantitative data (mean, median, mode, variance, SD)
resources.why_recommended: Comprehensive, exercise-backed Khan Academy unit covering all central-tendency and spread measures with immediate practice.

resources.title: Population and Estimated Parameters, Clearly Explained!!!
resources.why_recommended: Explains the crucial distinction between population parameters and sample estimates that underpins descriptive and inferential statistics.

resources.title: Covariance, Clearly Explained!!!
resources.why_recommended: StatQuest demystifies covariance step by step, showing exactly how it measures joint variability before moving to correlation.

resources.title: Pearson's Correlation, Clearly Explained!!!
resources.why_recommended: Clean explanation of the Pearson correlation coefficient and its relationship to covariance, essential for GATE data interpretation.

resources.title: RES.6-012 Introduction to Probability - Covariance, Correlation & Conditional Expectation
resources.why_recommended: Rigorous MIT treatment of covariance, correlation, and the law of iterated expectations / conditional variance needed for GATE.

topics.topic_name: Discrete Random Variables & Distributions (discrete uniform, Bernoulli, Binomial)

resources.title: The Binomial Distribution, Clearly Explained!!!
resources.why_recommended: Intuitive derivation of the binomial distribution from Bernoulli trials, exactly the discrete-distribution foundation GATE tests.

resources.title: Expected Values (Part 1): Discrete Random Variables
resources.why_recommended: Explains expected value for discrete random variables, directly supporting mean/variance computations for Bernoulli and binomial.

resources.title: RES.6-012 Introduction to Probability - Discrete Random Variables (Bernoulli, Binomial)
resources.why_recommended: Definitive coverage of PMFs, expectation and variance for discrete uniform, Bernoulli and binomial with problem sets.

topics.topic_name: Continuous Random Variables & Distributions (uniform, exponential, Poisson, normal)

resources.title: The Normal Distribution, Clearly Explained!!!
resources.why_recommended: StatQuest's clear intro to the normal (Gaussian) distribution, its parameters and shape, foundational for continuous distributions.

resources.title: RES.6-012 Introduction to Probability - Continuous RVs (uniform, exponential, normal)
resources.why_recommended: Rigorous MIT treatment of PDFs for uniform, exponential, Poisson and normal distributions, matching GATE's continuous-distribution depth.

resources.title: Why π is in the normal distribution (beyond integral tricks)
resources.why_recommended: Deep visual insight into the structure of the Gaussian; url points to the 3Blue1Brown Bayes lesson pending confirmation of the exact normal-distribution video id.

resources.title: An Introduction to the t Distribution (Includes some mathematical details)
resources.why_recommended: jbstatistics shows how the t distribution arises from a normal and chi-square, its PDF, and its relationship to the standard normal, exactly the sampling-distribution framing GATE needs.

resources.title: An Introduction to the Chi-Square Distribution
resources.why_recommended: Explains how the chi-square distribution arises from sums of squared standard normals, its PDF, mean, variance and shape, the sampling-distribution basis for chi-squared tests.

topics.topic_name: Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) & transformations of random variables

resources.title: RES.6-012 Introduction to Probability - CDFs & Derived Distributions
resources.why_recommended: MIT's units on CDFs and derived/transformed distributions (functions of a random variable) give the rigorous method GATE expects.

resources.title: Statistics 110: Probability - CDFs and Transformations of Random Variables
resources.why_recommended: Blitzstein covers CDFs and the change-of-variables/transformation technique with intuitive worked examples.

resources.title: But what is the Central Limit Theorem?
resources.why_recommended: 3Blue1Brown's visual masterclass on why sums of random variables converge to a Gaussian, building the deepest intuition for the CLT.

resources.title: The Central Limit Theorem, Clearly Explained!!!
resources.why_recommended: StatQuest gives a concise, practical statement of the CLT and why it justifies using normal-based inference on sample means.

resources.title: Sample means and the central limit theorem
resources.why_recommended: Khan Academy's sampling-distributions unit with CLT videos and practice problems reinforces the theory with hands-on exercises.

resources.title: Confidence Intervals, Clearly Explained!!!
resources.why_recommended: StatQuest clarifies what a confidence interval actually means using bootstrapping intuition, correcting the most common misconception.

resources.title: 18.05 Introduction to Probability and Statistics - Confidence Intervals
resources.instructor: Dr. Jeremy Orloff and Dr. Jennifer French Kamrin
resources.why_recommended: MIT 18.05 provides rigorous, exam-oriented notes and problem sets on confidence intervals for means and proportions.

resources.title: Hypothesis Testing and the Null Hypothesis, Clearly Explained!!!
resources.why_recommended: The clearest introduction to the logic of hypothesis testing and the null hypothesis, the mental model needed before z/t/chi-squared mechanics.

resources.title: p-values: What they are and how to interpret them
resources.why_recommended: Explains p-values correctly and how they drive accept/reject decisions in every hypothesis test, a frequent GATE conceptual trap.

resources.title: 18.05 Introduction to Probability and Statistics - Hypothesis Testing (z, t, chi-squared)
resources.instructor: Dr. Jeremy Orloff and Dr. Jennifer French Kamrin
resources.why_recommended: MIT 18.05 gives rigorous, worked treatments of z-tests, t-tests and chi-squared tests with problem sets aligned to GATE difficulty.
